state.title: include/fmt/format.h

part.text: The bug is in `write_nonfinite` (include/fmt/format.h:1589): with sign-aware zero padding (`align::numeric`), the padding is written before the sign because `left_padding_shifts[numeric] = 0` puts all fill on the left. I'll move the sign before the padding for numeric alignment.

The 'nan ' centered case works, but I need to verify how `{:+06}` with explicit fill/align combos parse in fmt to make sure `numeric` alignment only comes from `0` fill. Let me check the parser and then run the test suite.

part.text:
Fixed the issue where numeric zero fill was applied to inf/nan:

1. **include/fmt/format.h:1625** — `write_nonfinite` now replaces a `'0'` fill character with `' '`, so sign-aware zero padding has no effect on infinity/NaN while preserving width and alignment (e.g. `{:+06}` on NaN gives `"  +nan"` instead of `"00+nan"`).
2. **include/fmt/core.h:1950** — `on_zero()` no longer overrides an explicit alignment with `align::numeric`, so specs like `{:<+06}` keep their alignment (`"+nan  "`, `" +nan "`, `"  +nan"`).

Verified: `format-test` (including the previously failing `format_nan`/`format_infinity` cases), `format-impl-test`, `printf-test`, `chrono-test`, `core-test`, `assert-test`, `args-test`, `gtest-extra-test`, `ranges-test`, `os-test`, and `enforce-checks-test` all pass, and zero-padding for finite numbers (`{:+010.3}` → `+000000012`) is unchanged.
